full_judgment:
In this Rule the plaintiff petitioner challenged order No. 14 dated 30-5-2001 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sonagazi, Feni in Title Suit No. 46 of 2000 rejecting the petitioner's application for calling for the records of Title Suit No, 134 of 1958 and accordingly, the opposite party Nos. 1-4 were directed to show cause as to why the aforesaid order should not be set aside. 

 2. The plaintiff-petitioners case is that, they instituted Title Suit No. 46 of 2000 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sonagazi against the opposite parties for a decree declaring that the Solenama dated 13-2-62 and the Sole decree dated 2-6-62 passed on the basis of the said Solenama in Title Suit No. 134 of 1958 of the 1st Court of Munsif, Feni, as shown in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint of the present suit is forged, fraudulent, false, collusive, ineffective, illegal, null and void and not binding upon the petitioners and also prayed for setting aside the said Sole decree. 

 3. The case of the plaintiff-petitioners, in short, is that the petitioners had no knowledge about Title Suit No, 134 of 1952 as they were never served with any summons of the said suit nor they have filed any vokalatnama in the said suit to contest the same and, as such, a solenama shown to have been filed therein on the basis of which the Sole decree was obtained is fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon them. It is the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-4 who practiced fraud upon the Court and filed the alleged Solenama by forging the thumb impressions and signatures of the predecessor of the petitioners, The predecessors of the petitioners having right, title, interest and possession in the suit property never knew about such Sole decree. The present defendant Nos. 1-4 recently brought Title Suit No. 30 of 2000 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Feni for partition of the land of the concerned khatian. On receiving the notice of that suit the petitioners came to know about Title Suit No. 134 of 1958 and about the solenama foiled therein allegedly by their, predecessors and the Sole decree dated 2-6-62 passed in the said suit. Their specific case is that the thumb impressions and the signatures of the predecessors of the petitioners contained in the solenama are all forged, false and, as such, the sole decree obtained on the basis of such false and forged document filed in Title Suit No. 134 of 1958 is illegal, void and not binding upon the present plaintiff-petitioners. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1-4 filed written statement in the suit denying the material allegations of the plaint contending, inter alia, that the entire property originally belonged to three brothers, the predecessors of the petitioners and the contesting defendant opposite parties, the numbers of co-sharers being increased the names of all the co-sharers were not recorded in the Khatian. However, the subsequent purchasers instituted Title Suit No. 134 of 1958 wherein an application for addition of co-plaintiffs was filed on 19-2-1959 and subsequent thereto a solenama was filed on 13-2-1962 on the basis of which a sole decree was passed on 2-6-62. The parties to the decree are possessing their respective sahams on the basis of the said sole decree. The suit, being hit by limitation are res judicata, is thus liable to be dismissed. 

 5. However, the plaintiff-petitioners found it absolutely necessary to bring before the court the relevant materials of Title Suit No. 134 of 1958 upon which fraud and forgery were practiced by the predecessors of the defendant-opposite parties and obtained the so-called sole decree. The petitioners claimed that this is very much essential in the present suit and the original documents bearing the mark and elements of the fraud and forgery are necessary to prove the present case, thus an application was filed accordingly. 

 6. The learned Assistant Judge, upon hearing the parties and perusing the said application, was pleased to reject the same by his order dated 29-4-2001 holding that the plaintiffs will be able to prove their case upon obtaining and filing the certified copies of the relevant documents. The plaintiff-petitioners thereafter on 20-5-2001 filed another application stating the fact that the certified copy of all the documents have already been filed but the certified copy will not be of any assistance to prove the forgery and fraud practiced by the predecessor of the defendants because the original document contains concerned thumb impressions and the signatures, which cannot be ascertained from the certified copies. Accordingly, the plaintiff petitioner prayed for recalling the order dated 29-4-2001 and allow the application for calling for the record of Title Suit No. 134 of 1958, 

 8. Mrs. Ferdousi Sahab, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the learned Assistant Judge committed an error resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in rejecting the application without considering that the alleged fraud cannot be determined or proved without the original document being produced before the Court. In that respect the solenama filed in Title Suit No. 134 of 1958 being the subject matter, where the allegation of fraud and forgery has been made, is the basis of the present suit and until and unless the original document is brought before the Court fraud and forgery cannot be proved in accordance with law, Thus the plaintiff-petitioners will not be able to succeed in the present suit. Accordingly, the rejection of application has caused error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. She further submits that the Court below misconstrued the law and fact and accordingly, observed in the earlier order that the certified copy will be sufficient to prove the plaintiffs case on the basis of the facts and circumstances of the case, such observation is not tenable in law. 

 11. On the perusal of the same it appears that the present suit is for declaration that the solenama and the sole decree passed in Title Suit No. 134 of 1958 are forged, fraudulent and non binding upon the plaintiff and also for setting aside the said sole decree. The specific case of the plaintiff-petitioners is that fraud has been practiced by forging the thumb impressions and signatures of the predecessors of the present petitioners and the alleged solenama has been filed only to obtain a sole decree which is the subject matter of the present suit. To ascertain whether fraud and forgery has been practiced the original document is very much essential and accordingly, the application was filed for calling the record of the concerned suit containing the said original document The finding of the trial Court that the allegation of the plaintiff-petitioners can be proved by filing the certified copies of the documents seems to be a misconceived one because the certified copy of the document does not contain the original thumb impressions or signatures of the parties. Accordingly, it cannot be ascertained from the copies whether the same are genuine or forged. On perusal of the impugned order it appears that the same has been rejected on the ground that the same prayer was rejected earlier by order dated 29-4-2001 and, as such, there is no scope for entertaining the present application.
